1.explanation:
• cli.md: shows how to reproduce the issue via the prettier CLI with the --parser babel flag, matching the bug report’s invocation.  
• api.md: documents the programmatic API (format and resolveConfig) and parser option so you can reproduce the bug in a script or Playground.  
• options.md: lists the parser, printWidth, tabWidth, and other options that can affect JSX formatting and whitespace handling.  
• technical-details.md: explains the internal printing/line-breaking algorithm and how whitespace nodes are handled in the Babel printer, which is where the U+3000 space bug originates.  
• integrating-with-linters.md: covers how Prettier is run under ESLint (the user runs yarn lint in the GIF), showing how the same underlying formatting rules apply in editor/CI environments.  
• editors.md: describes editor integrations (e.g., VS Code) so you can verify the bug in your IDE and see how the extension invokes Prettier under the hood.
1.bug_scenario:
The bug occurs when a full-width Japanese space (Unicode U+3000) is embedded in a JSX return between self-closing tags and a JSX expression ({this.props.data.title}). Prettier 1.19.1 sometimes moves or mis-indents the full-width space onto its own line, or shifts its indentation incorrectly. In the GIF, you can see the space jumping before the expression or getting an extra leading space on a separate line, despite no configuration changes. The affected elements are the opening

tag, the two components, the full-width spaces around the title expression, and the code’s indentation in the JSX tree.
